# Test fixtures

Fixtures are synthetic only. They contain no real infrastructure data. Values use obvious
markers such as `SYNTHETIC-...`.

Golden files (in `pkg/report/testdata/`) are refreshed only with `go test ./pkg/report -update`,
and every diff must be reviewed against `specs/001-baseline-cli-behavior/contracts/cli-contract.md`.

## Terraform version

The hand-written fixtures in `plans/` use `terraform_version` `1.17.2`, the newest stable release listed on
https://releases.hashicorp.com/terraform/ (checked 2026-11-25).

Supported series could not be confirmed from HashiCorp's official source: the support-policy
page (`developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/docs/support-period-and-end-of-life-policy`)
returned HTTP 404 on 2026-11-25. The releases index lists the series 1.17, 1.16, 1.15, 1.14,
1.13, 1.12, 1.11, 1.10 and 1.9 (latest patches 1.17.2, 1.16.7, 1.15.9, 1.14.9, 1.13.5, 1.12.2,
1.11.4, 1.10.5, 1.9.8) but does not state which are supported. The choice of 1.17.2 was
confirmed by the maintainer.

The authentic plans in `plans/terraform/` carry the version of the Terraform binary that generated
them (see below), because they are the verbatim output of `terraform show -json`.

| Fixture | terraform_version | format_version | purpose |

## Authentic plans

`plans/terraform/*.json` (Terraform 1.10.5) and `plans/opentofu/*.json` (OpenTofu 1.9.0) are real
`show -json` outputs, generated by `scripts/gen-plans.sh` (`make fixtures`) from the scenarios in
`scenarios/<name>/`. The script removes the non-deterministic `timestamp` and replaces generated UUIDs
with a fixed value, so regenerating with the same versions gives the same files. It needs `jq` and the
engine binaries; an engine that is not installed is skipped.

A scenario holds `plan/` (the configuration that is planned, possibly with a hand-written
`terraform.tfstate`), optionally `base/` (applied first to build a prior state), `flags` (extra plan
flags), `taint` (addresses tainted after the base apply) and `engines` (engines to run, default both).

Two kinds of scenarios:

- **Built-in resource only.** `terraform_data` needs no provider download, no network and no credential.
- **Real providers.** `aws`, `google`, `kubernetes`, `github` and `random`/`local` are pinned to exact
  versions and configured with synthetic credentials, so that planning needs no account and no call to a
  cloud API. The first run downloads the providers from the registry of the engine (about 1 GB, kept in
  `~/.cache/tf2report/plugins`, or `PLUGIN_CACHE`).

Scenarios on `terraform_data`, run by both engines:

| Scenario | counted changes | purpose |
|----------|-----------------|---------|
| `mixed-actions` | add 1, change 1, destroy 1, replace 1, 1 ignored | every action in one plan, with an output change and `delete_because_no_resource_config` |
| `create-before-destroy` | replace 1 | replacement ordered `["create","delete"]` |
| `forced-replace` | replace 2, 1 ignored | `replace_by_request` (`-replace`) and `replace_because_tainted` |
| `destroy-all` | destroy 3 | `plan -destroy` |
| `moved` | change 1, 1 ignored | `moved` blocks: `previous_address`, a move with a change and a pure move |
| `import` | change 1 | `import` block, `importing` in the change |
| `count-for-each` | add 8 | `count` indexes and `for_each` keys with spaces, quotes and non-ASCII characters |
| `nested-modules` | add 7 | nested modules, `count` and `for_each` on modules |
| `sensitive` | add 1 | sensitive variable and output |
| `data-source` | add 1, 1 ignored | data source deferred to apply (`mode: data`, action `read`) |
| `no-changes` | none, 2 ignored | all resources up to date (`no-op`) |
| `empty-config` | none | configuration without a resource: `resource_changes` is absent |

Scenarios on real providers:

| Scenario | Engines | counted changes | purpose |
|----------|---------|-----------------|---------|
| `provider-multi-create` | terraform | add 4 | AWS, Google, Kubernetes and GitHub (`integrations` namespace) in one plan |
| `provider-multi-actions` | terraform | add 1, change 1, destroy 1, replace 1, 1 ignored | all actions chosen by the provider schema, from a hand-written prior state planned with `-refresh=false` |
| `provider-nested-blocks` | terraform | add 3 | nested blocks, sets and `jsonencode` (security group, IAM policy, instance) |
| `provider-sensitive` | terraform | add 1 | sensitive attribute of a real provider schema |
| `provider-random` | both | add 4 | same providers through two registries: `registry.terraform.io` and `registry.opentofu.org` |
| `opentofu-provider-for-each` | opentofu | add 3 | provider instances created with `for_each`, an OpenTofu feature |

Providers that could not be planned offline are absent: Datadog validates resources through its API at
plan time, and `azurerm` authenticates against Microsoft Entra before planning.

Known Gap: every plan that creates or deletes a resource carries `before_sensitive: false` or
`after_sensitive: false`, which the parser rejects today (see `real-shape.json`). That includes all
real-provider plans. They are pinned by provisional tests, and their counting logic is still verified
once the unreadable flags are removed. The tests also list every file of these directories, so a new
scenario must be classified.

## Diagram fixtures

`plans/diagram/` holds synthetic plans in the real `terraform show -json` shape, with a `configuration`
section, for the `svg` format. Every attribute value in them is an invented marker.

- `aws-network.json`: vpc (no-op), subnet (create), instance (update), security group (replace), bucket
  (delete) and a `count = 2` instance; every status once, references between resources.
- `azure-network.json`: resource group, virtual network, subnet, VM and storage account (create, update,
  delete) with references.
- `gcp-network.json`: network, subnetwork, instance, bucket and SQL instance (create, update, replace),
  including a `depends_on`.
- `modules-context.json`: a module output reference, an unchanged resource referenced by a changed one
  (dependency context), an unreferenced unchanged one, a `count` module pair and a `random` resource.
- `cycle.json`: two resources that reference each other, plus an independent one.
- `no-configuration.json`: valid plan without a `configuration` key (older format version).

## Volume

No large file is committed. `pkg/report/scale_test.go` builds a 5 000-change plan in memory (seven
resource types, names with spaces, quotes and non-ASCII characters, every action including no-op, read
and empty) and checks counts, ordering and determinism. `go test ./pkg/report -bench FormatLargePlan`
measures 10 000 changes.

## Examples

`examples/` at the repository root holds plans only, as a copy of fixtures that the tool can read. The
test in `cmd/tf2report/examples_test.go` keeps them in sync with this directory.
